**Trusting a project**: The first time you open a project with hooks, you must trust it before its project hooks will run; until then they are silently skipped. Grant trust by running `/hooks-trust` (or launching with `--trust`); the decision is recorded in the unified folder-trust store (`~/.grok/trusted_folders.toml`), the same gate that governs repo-local MCP/LSP servers. Global hooks in `~/.grok/hooks/` are always trusted and need no entry. This prevents untrusted repos from running arbitrary code.

Because hooks are unified under folder-trust, a `--trust` / `/hooks-trust` grant trusts the whole folder for **MCP, LSP, and hooks** together, and covers subdirectories of the same repository. A nested git checkout under that folder is a separate workspace and is not covered. Conversely, disabling folder-trust (`GROK_FOLDER_TRUST=0` or `[folder_trust] enabled = false`) ungates project hooks along with MCP/LSP.

Event types:
| Type               | Description                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`             | A chunk of the agent's response text                                                          |
| `thought`          | Internal reasoning (thinking tokens)                                                          |
| `tool_call`        | A tool call the agent started (`toolCallId`, `toolName`, `kind`, `status`, `rawInput`, `content`, `locations`) |
| `tool_call_update` | Progress or result for a tool call (`status`, `rawOutput`, `content`, `locations`)            |
| `usage`            | Per-response boundary (`messageId`, `stopReason`, `usage`, `signature`), one per model response |
| `plan`             | The agent's current plan (`entries`)                                                          |
| `available_commands` | Tool and slash command lists (`tools`, `commands`)                                          |
| `end`              | Final event with metadata and spend fields when available                                    |
| `error`            | An error occurred (carries `message`, and spend fields if any)                         
      |
`end` is always the last event. Spend fields on `end` match the json object
shape (snake_case uncached `input_tokens`, safe cost floats). `end.stopReason`
is the turn stop reason in snake_case (`end_turn`, `max_tokens`,
`max_turn_requests`, `refusal`, `cancelled`); the verbatim per-response provider
reason (e.g. `tool_use`, `pause_turn`) is on the `usage` line's `stopReason`.
Per-response `message_id`/`stopReason`/`signature` are populated on the Messages
API backend; other backends report what they carry.
Grok may also emit `max_turns_reached` and `auto_compact_*` events; treat the list as non-exhaustive and switch on `type`.
### streaming-messages-json
Newline-delimited JSON in the Messages API `stream-json` wire format. The data-bearing surface matches the Messages shape exactly. This includes the `assistant`/`user` message bodies, `usage`, `tool_use`/`tool_result`, inline web search, `stop_reason`, and the `--include-partial-messages` event framing. A consumer that reconstructs messages, reads spend, or detects errors works without changes.
The `system`/`init` and terminal `result` lines carry metadata. Grok emits the fields it has real data for and omits pure-placeholder fields it cannot fill, rather than zero-filling them. As a result, those two lines may not pass strict `init`/`result'

import subprocess,re

for f in --compaction-mode --storage-mode --append-system-prompt --leader --no-leader \
         --oauth --no-memory --experimental-memory --memory-flush --trust --print \
         --hunk-tracker-mode --background-wait-timeout --no-wait-for-background \
         --xai-api-base-url --cli-chat-proxy-base-url --grok-ws-url --grok-ws-origin \
         --client-identifier --load --reauth --device-auth --device-code \
         --subagents --plan --add-dir --dangerously-skip-permissions --yolo \
         --hostname-bin --workers --keep-data --plugin-dir --agent-profile \
         --no-auto-update --auto --dontAsk --acceptEdits; do
  echo "----- $f -----"
  grok "$f" help 2>&1 | head -8
done

echo
echo '===== --help long: look for Hidden ====='
# clap sometimes shows hidden with GROK_DEBUG or --help-hidden; try both
grok --help-hidden 2>&1 | head -5
echo
# dump ALL long-option names clap knows by feeding a unique junk value after --
python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess,re
# Use grok --help (full) 
p=subprocess.run(['grok','--help'],capture_output=True,text=True)
print('--- documented options ---')
flags=sorted(set(re.findall(r'(?:^|\s)(-{1,2}[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*)', p.stdout)))
for f in flags:
    print(f)
print('count',len(flags))
PY

rawOutput.command:
# Kill any hung interactive grok from the previous probe
pkill -f 'grok --' 2>/dev/null || true
# Probe remaining hidden flags non-interactively: always pass a dummy so clap errors before TUI
probe() {
  local f="$1"
  local out
  out=$(grok "$f" 2>&1 | head -c 300)
  if echo "$out" | grep -q "unexpected argument"; then
    echo "UNKNOWN	$f	$(echo "$out" | tr '\n' ' ' | head -c 140)"
  else
    echo "ACCEPT 	$f	$(echo "$out" | tr '\n' ' ' | head -c 180)"
  fi
}
for f in --fs-write --fs-read --no-ask-user --ask-user --load --save --client-identifier \
         --subagents --plan --add-dir --additional-dirs --additional-directories \
         --print --trust --no-trust --folder-trust \
         --compaction-mode=off --storage-mode=off --storage-mode=workspace \
         --no-memory --experimental-memory --memory-flush \
         --leader --no-leader --oauth --append-system-prompt=x \
         --hostname-bin --workers --keep-data --plugin-dir=/tmp \
         --agent-profile=/tmp --xai-api-base-url=http://x --cli-chat-proxy-base-url=http://x \
         --grok-ws-url=http://x --reauth --device-auth --device-code \
         --auto --dontAsk --acceptEdits --bypassPermissions \
         --yolo --dangerously-skip-permissions \
         --no-auto-update --help-hidden \
         -a -t -A -d -n -f -l -u -x -y -z -q -b -e -g -i -j -k; do
  probe "$f"
done

rawOutput.command:
# Kill any hung interactive grok from the previous probe
pkill -f 'grok --' 2>/dev/null || true
# Probe remaining hidden flags non-interactively: always pass a dummy so clap errors before TUI
probe() {
  local f="$1"
  local out
  out=$(grok "$f" 2>&1 | head -c 300)
  if echo "$out" | grep -q "unexpected argument"; then
    echo "UNKNOWN	$f	$(echo "$out" | tr '\n' ' ' | head -c 140)"
  else
    echo "ACCEPT 	$f	$(echo "$out" | tr '\n' ' ' | head -c 180)"
  fi
}
for f in --fs-write --fs-read --no-ask-user --ask-user --load --save --client-identifier \
         --subagents --plan --add-dir --additional-dirs --additional-directories \
         --print --trust --no-trust --folder-trust \
         --compaction-mode=off --storage-mode=off --storage-mode=workspace \
         --no-memory --experimental-memory --memory-flush \
         --leader --no-leader --oauth --append-system-prompt=x \
         --hostname-bin --workers --keep-data --plugin-dir=/tmp \
         --agent-profile=/tmp --xai-api-base-url=http://x --cli-chat-proxy-base-url=http://x \
         --grok-ws-url=http://x --reauth --device-auth --device-code \
         --auto --dontAsk --acceptEdits --bypassPermissions \
         --yolo --dangerously-skip-permissions \
         --no-auto-update --help-hidden \
         -a -t -A -d -n -f -l -u -x -y -z -q -b -e -g -i -j -k; do
  probe "$f"
done

rawOutput.command:
# Kill any hung interactive grok from the previous probe
pkill -f 'grok --' 2>/dev/null || true
# Probe remaining hidden flags non-interactively: always pass a dummy so clap errors before TUI
probe() {
  local f="$1"
  local out
  out=$(grok "$f" 2>&1 | head -c 300)
  if echo "$out" | grep -q "unexpected argument"; then
    echo "UNKNOWN	$f	$(echo "$out" | tr '\n' ' ' | head -c 140)"
  else
    echo "ACCEPT 	$f	$(echo "$out" | tr '\n' ' ' | head -c 180)"
  fi
}
for f in --fs-write --fs-read --no-ask-user --ask-user --load --save --client-identifier \
         --subagents --plan --add-dir --additional-dirs --additional-directories \
         --print --trust --no-trust --folder-trust \
         --compaction-mode=off --storage-mode=off --storage-mode=workspace \
         --no-memory --experimental-memory --memory-flush \
         --leader --no-leader --oauth --append-system-prompt=x \
         --hostname-bin --workers --keep-data --plugin-dir=/tmp \
         --agent-profile=/tmp --xai-api-base-url=http://x --cli-chat-proxy-base-url=http://x \
         --grok-ws-url=http://x --reauth --device-auth --device-code \
         --auto --dontAsk --acceptEdits --bypassPermissions \
         --yolo --dangerously-skip-permissions \
         --no-auto-update --help-hidden \
         -a -t -A -d -n -f -l -u -x -y -z -q -b -e -g -i -j -k; do
  probe "$f"
done

# Kill any hung interactive grok from the previous probe
pkill -f 'grok --' 2>/dev/null || true
# Probe remaining hidden flags non-interactively: always pass a dummy so clap errors before TUI
probe() {
  local f="$1"
  local out
  out=$(grok "$f" 2>&1 | head -c 300)
  if echo "$out" | grep -q "unexpected argument"; then
    echo "UNKNOWN	$f	$(echo "$out" | tr '\n' ' ' | head -c 140)"
  else
    echo "ACCEPT 	$f	$(echo "$out" | tr '\n' ' ' | head -c 180)"
  fi
}
for f in --fs-write --fs-read --no-ask-user --ask-user --load --save --client-identifier \
         --subagents --plan --add-dir --additional-dirs --additional-directories \
         --print --trust --no-trust --folder-trust \
         --compaction-mode=off --storage-mode=off --storage-mode=workspace \
         --no-memory --experimental-memory --memory-flush \
         --leader --no-leader --oauth --append-system-prompt=x \
         --hostname-bin --workers --keep-data --plugin-dir=/tmp \
         --agent-profile=/tmp --xai-api-base-url=http://x --cli-chat-proxy-base-url=http://x \
         --grok-ws-url=http://x --reauth --device-auth --device-code \
         --auto --dontAsk --acceptEdits --bypassPermissions \

         --no-auto-update --help-hidden \
         -a -t -A -d -n -f -l -u -x -y -z -q -b -e -g -i -j -k; do
  probe "$f"
done
